transcript.text: Every so often when I put the washing machine on the whole kitchen power goes off and I have to go to the fuse box and flick the switch back up. It doesn't happen every time. Indesit, IWE 7 something.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Please don't keep resetting the trip. Leave the appliance unplugged and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer before using it again. This is a safety issue: please stop using the washing machine until an engineer has checked it. Repeatedly resetting the fuse box can be dangerous if there is an earth fault inside the appliance. The most common cause for this symptom in Indesit machines is the heater element developing a short to earth, which trips the RCD when the heating stage begins. Less commonly, it could be the drain pump or the mains wiring. To help narrow this down safely: does the power trip immediately when you turn the dial on, or only once the machine has started filling with water and begins to heat it up?

It doesn't trip as soon as I turn it on. It's always a few minutes into a 40 or 60 degree wash, and it has never tripped on a cold wash, a quick 30 or a rinse and spin. It happens roughly 1 in 4 washes over the last month. I'll admit I've been resetting the switch each time, so it has tripped quite a few times now. I haven't smelled burning or seen any sparks.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Please don't keep resetting the trip. Leave the appliance unplugged and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer before using it again. That pattern—tripping only on hot washes, never on cold ones—is classic for a heating element developing a short to earth. The RCD trips because electricity is leaking from the live/heating circuit into the metal casing when it gets hot. There's a risk of damage or fire if that fault worsens. I need you to check the heater element safely (unplugged) by testing for continuity between its terminals and the casing; if it shows any connection, the element is faulty and needs replacing. If it tests fine, we'll look at the drain pump next.

I'm afraid I can't do that test. I don't have a multimeter or any kind of insulation tester, and I'm not comfortable working on the internal wiring of the machine. I'll leave it unplugged as you say. Should I get an electrician or an appliance engineer in to test the element?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
You should get an appliance engineer. An electrician checks your home wiring and fuse box, but they won't open up or test the washing machine itself; only a qualified appliance engineer can safely diagnose and check the faulty heating element inside the machine. Given that it trips specifically when heating is engaged, the heater element is the most likely culprit, as these often develop an internal short to the metal casing over time. Please do not attempt to use the machine again until this has been resolved.
